headline: The morning showers are over and every model is now completely dry for the next 72 hours, so the street's rating stays at none; the main hazard is Thursday's 12:35 PM king tide on the Bay shore, under a Coastal Flood Warning until 4 PM Thursday.

summary.text: Down since this morning: the showers ended, and HRRR (0.09 in), NBM (0.08 in) and RRFS (0.03 in) all dropped to 0.00 in. No rain in any model through Saturday evening.
Wettest 3 hours, next 72 h: HRRR, HRRR 15-minute, RRFS, NBM, ECMWF and GFS all 0.00 in. Full agreement on a dry Thanksgiving through Saturday.
Rating card consensus 0.00 in: none. No rain means no street flooding from storm runoff. Yellow (garage) would need about 0.71 in in 3 hours.
Dry through Saturday with patchy night and morning fog. NWS expects rain to return Sunday, highest chances Sunday evening, and a likely stronger storm late Monday into Tuesday.
King tide Thursday: 9.4 ft at 12:35 PM, NOAA's model about 10.8 ft with surge. Channel at Alameda 0.14 ft at 4 PM, far below Flood Monitoring 3.18 ft.
No need to move cars. Stay off the Bay shore, sloughs and shoreline roads around 11 AM to 2 PM Thursday. Use Friday and Saturday to clear drain grates before Sunday.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text:
The post-frontal showers tapered off this morning, followed by low clouds and patchy valley fog. NWS San Francisco's afternoon discussion (12:29 PM short and long term, 4:04 PM aviation) expects partly cloudy, quiet weather through Saturday under weak ridging, with a persistent stream of high clouds, near to slightly above average temperatures (low 60s along the Bay), and a good chance of patchy, locally dense fog tonight and Thursday and Friday nights in the inland valleys.

The storm door reopens Sunday: NWS expects increasing rain chances through the day Sunday with the highest chances Sunday evening (slight, about 20 %, chance of thunderstorms), showers Monday, then a second, likely stronger storm beginning late Monday with the heaviest rain Tuesday. NWS's first-wave estimate for cities around San Francisco Bay is 0.25 to 1 in through Monday morning. This is beyond the 72-hour window the models on this page cover.

The Coastal Flood Warning for San Francisco and San Pablo Bay shorelines was reissued at 3:54 PM and runs until 4 PM Thursday.

sections.title: What changed and model trends
sections.text:
Since the 4:25 AM discussion the last showers came through and moved out, and every model has dropped to zero. This morning HRRR showed 0.09 in in 3 hours, the HRRR 15-minute series 0.23 in, NBM 0.08 in and RRFS 0.03 in; all are now 0.00 in.

Wettest 3 hours / total, from 4 PM Wednesday (72 hours):
• HRRR (2 PM Wed run, out to 10 AM Fri): 0.00 / 0.00 in.
• HRRR 15-minute (ends 11:45 PM Thu): 0.00 in.
• RRFS (4 AM Wed run): 0.00 / 0.00 in.
• NBM: 0.00 / 0.00 in.
• ECMWF: 0.00 / 0.00 in.
• GFS: 0.00 / 0.00 in.

Consensus (HRRR × 1.25, RRFS, NBM): 0.00 in, matching the rating card at none. With all six sources in agreement there is nothing to second-guess for the next three days. The model series on this page end Saturday night, so Sunday's system is not yet in them.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
NOAA's Bay model (run ends 7 AM Friday) still runs about 1.0 to 1.6 ft above the predicted tides at Redwood City. Today's 9.5 ft king tide at 11:46 AM was modeled at about 11.1 ft near noon.

Ahead: tonight's -1.7 ft low at 7:17 PM runs about -0.4 ft near 8 PM. Thursday: 7.1 ft high at 2:08 AM (about 8.5 ft), 3.3 ft low at 7:06 AM (about 4.4 ft), and the 9.4 ft high at 12:35 PM (about 10.8 ft near 1 PM). Friday's 9.1 ft high is at 1:28 PM and Saturday's 8.6 ft high at 2:27 PM.

NWS: at the San Francisco gauge Thursday's high is expected 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW at 11:38 AM), including up to 1.5 ft of surge, approaching the highest tide ever recorded there, with up to 2.5 ft of inundation possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. Highs stay about 2.0 ft above normal Friday and Saturday. These tides matter for the Bay shore and tidal sloughs, not for Athlone Terrace directly; with no rain forecast they will not back up the channel at the street.

Channel: at Alameda de las Pulgas 0.14 ft at 4 PM, steady between 0.12 and 0.15 ft all day (Flood Monitoring 3.18 ft, Watch 4.6 ft, Warning 5.65 ft). Upstream of Caltrain: 0.07 ft at 5:13 AM, its latest report (Flood Monitoring 2.8 ft).

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: Dry. The Caltrain rain gauge's latest report (5:13 AM) showed no rain in the preceding 24 hours, and it has not reported since, so there is still no local measurement of this morning's showers. The Alameda channel gauge barely moved all day (0.12 to 0.15 ft), consistent with only light rain locally. NWS reports partly cloudy skies, cirrus moving in, and fog and low clouds redeveloping tonight.

sections.title: Uncertainty
sections.text: Very low for the next three days: all models agree on no rain. The uncertainty now is Sunday through Tuesday. NWS has at least moderate confidence in a soaking rain (widespread over 0.25 in) for the Bay Area with the second storm, but notes the surface low could come ashore anywhere from San Francisco to Point Conception, which could raise or lower totals here. The Caltrain gauges' 11-hour reporting gap is worth watching before that storm.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• Tonight and Thursday morning: nothing needed on the street; no need to move cars out of the cul-de-sac. Watch for dense fog if driving for Thanksgiving.
• Thursday around 11 AM to 2 PM: stay away from the Bay shore, tidal sloughs and low shoreline roads during the king tide; don't walk or drive through moving water. Friday's early-afternoon high is nearly as high.
• Friday and Saturday: clear leaves from street drain grates and yard drains, check sandbags, and secure outdoor decorations before Sunday's rain and the stronger storm Monday night into Tuesday.
